findings.passage: Protect the armed body of the people from both federal overreach and state-level disarmament — the right to keep and bear arms and the duty of common defense are two faces of one design.
findings.note: Third item of the plan under the 'Second Amendment: Restore the Militia' plank on his campaign issues section.
subjects: oppose state limits on gun ownership

findings.passage: Federal policy should defend the armed citizen against both federal overreach and state-level disarmament of the very body from which the militia is drawn.
findings.note: Part C of the proposal in his Second Amendment position paper on his campaign site.
subjects: oppose state limits on gun ownership

findings.passage: A people forbidden the ordinary arms of a citizen cannot constitute the militia the Constitution presupposes.
findings.note: From Part C of the same position paper, on why he opposes limits on the arms ordinary citizens may own.

findings.passage: In May 2026, Virginia enacted a ban on the future sale, purchase, and manufacture of the most common semi-automatic rifles in America — Virginia, whose own Declaration of Rights, adopted June 12, 1776 in George Mason’s hand, was among the first inscriptions of the principle this paper defends:
findings.note: In the position paper he describes Virginia's 2026 ban on new sales of semi-automatic rifles as states moving 'to disarm the body of the people'; the paper then says the state 'has now legislated against its premise'.
